sections.content:
13,430 people

were counted on the census as "clinical psychologists" in England and Wales in March 2021.

Clinical psychologists work with people experiencing emotional, psychological or behavioural distress, perform tests and assess their emotional, cognitive and behavioural processes, and determine treatments to help patients improve their mental wellbeing.

More women than men had this job

Among people working as "clinical psychologists" there were more women than men (83.1% compared with 16.9%).

This means "clinical psychologists" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "health professionals".

Men made up 16.9% and women made up 83.1% of "clinical psychologists"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "clinical psychologists" included:

  • other psychologists
  • clothing, fashion and accessories designers
  • social workers

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

How old are people who do this job?

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 30 to 34 years. Of the whole working population 12% were aged 30 to 34 years. For people working as "clinical psychologists", 19.4% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "clinical psychologists" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "clinical psychologists" included:

  • research and development (r&d) managers
  • dental practitioners
  • sales accounts and business development managers

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "clinical psychologists", 9.4% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had more people aged between 30 and 49 years compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (63.5% compared with 36.5%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (86.7%) than self-employed (13.3%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was London. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Sheffield, this is in the region of the Yorkshire & Humberside.
